_readme: THE machine-checked house style. gates.py reads this file, not the prose in
SKILL.md or references/*.md. If a rule is not in here, no gate enforces it and
the next agent will re-derive it differently — which is exactly how a build
shipped with ASS-box pills and 62pt outlined captions while every gate passed.
A project may override any top-level key by writing work_dir/house_style.local.json.
An override is allowed but must be WRITTEN DOWN — a deliberate exemption, not a
gap. gates.py prints every active override so a reviewer sees it.
`python3 gates.py --preflight` prints this as a build checklist. Run it BEFORE

font.note: resolve via modules/title.py _find_font(); the .ass Fontname must match

captions.note: Outline 0 + Shadow >= 5 is a drop shadow, NEVER a black outline.

keyword.note: Gold keyword spans — numbers/product names pop gold at 90px inside white 84px lines. Colour is the user-locked #F6DB66 (ASS BBGGRR), superseding the older &H5AD6F5 in running-vlog-template §11. min_spans guards the failure shipped 2026-08-17: a full caption pass rendered pure white because nothing checked for the gold layer at all.

captions.min_dwell_note: Shortest a caption may stay on screen. plan.py has carried MIN_CAPTION_S = 1.8 as advice since the beginning and NO gate enforced it, so a 0.75s caption that nobody can finish reading shipped with every gate green (2026-08-19).

pill.centre_pct_note: Raised from 0.23 to 0.18 on 2026-08-19 at the user's request ('以後都在往上一點') — a standing preference for every future build, not a one-off.
pill.note: modules/title.py render_title_png. NOT drawn in ASS — an ASS opaque box has square corners, which the corner_alpha_max check is what detects.

cover.note: The subtitle is sized to the TITLE's rendered width so the two read as one block. title_max_w_ratio caps the font sizer's ADVANCE width; the italic house font's ink runs a little past that, hence title_ink_overhang_tol_px.
cover.subtitle_gold_note: Locked by the user 2026-08-16: EVERY cover subtitle is this yellow. modules/cover.py reads it via _house_gold(); do not pass a literal colour.
cover.subtitle_min_pt_note: The subtitle is width-matched to the title, so a SHORT title plus a LONG subtitle silently crushes it. Calibrated on two measured covers rather than picked: a 3-character title (600px) with a 15-character subtitle rendered 42pt (4.7px at IG grid width) and the user could not see it at all, while a 2-line title with a 15-character subtitle rendered 56pt (6.2px) and reads fine — checked by rendering it at grid size and looking. The line sits between them, nearer the failure. A first pass at 64 would have blocked the 56pt cover, which is tuning the world to fit the threshold. Below this cover.draw() raises: the answer is fewer characters, never a smaller size.

bilingual.note: Off by default. A project that wants an English line sets required:true in work_dir/house_style.local.json, and then EVERY caption must carry one — half-translated is the failure this catches.

music.note: How long the music bed may be inaudible at the END of the video. It must be LONGER than the intended fade-out, or the gate fights the fade; it must be well SHORT of the 2.2-2.7s that shipped as 'the music cut out'. Measured by differencing the music version against its -nomusic sibling, so it needs both files.
music.duck_note: How much quieter the bed must be under speech than away from it, measured by differencing the music render against its no-music sibling. buildkit.duck_mix used an ABSOLUTE trigger (peak > 0.12) tuned for one close mic; on a room with speakers at several distances it ducked the close mic 7-9 dB and the room-distance speakers only 2-3 dB, while ducking 8.5 dB under paper being turned. Nothing measured it, so a user caught it instead of a gate.
music.max_silent_head_s_note: HOUSE RULE (user, 2026-08-21): the hook gets music. Not a fade from nothing and not silence — the bed comes in with the opening, at a level that sits alongside whatever is on the hook's own audio, and then carries into the main section. Holding the bed back entirely is reserved for a genuinely exceptional voice moment. The reason is simple and it is what prompted this: when the opening has no voice and no music either, it has no feeling, and the viewer decides in those seconds whether the video has a soundtrack at all. Measured as MASKING, not signal: a bed 20 dB under a loud room is present in the arithmetic and gone to the ear, and a dropout-style floor calls it live. 'Why is there no music at the start' was reported on two separate edits and passed every gate both times, because max_dead_tail_s watches the END and nothing watched the beginning. The rare exception goes on record rather than being assumed: decisions.json music.head = 'cold_open' with a why. If you find yourself writing that often, the duck is misfiring, not the rule.

pacing.note: Floor on a single shot's screen time. Measured 2026-08-25 over every finished timeline in reach — six cuts across three folders — whose shortest shots were 1.30 1.40 1.50 1.70 2.30 2.30; the beat-synced running-vlog reference in references/examples/ bottoms out at 1.50s. Nothing anybody kept has gone below 1.3s. The round-B build the viewer called 「很不順、跳」 had a 0.20s shot, and review.py had been printing shortest_s all along without grading it — the same shape as plan.py carrying MIN_CAPTION_S as advice until a 0.75s caption shipped green. 1.2 sits below every kept cut on purpose: this says 'nobody has ever done this and got away with it', not 'this is wrong'. A deliberate faster cut lowers it in house_style.local.json, which gates.py prints. NO cuts-per-second ceiling here: at min_shot_s=1.2 every legal shot already forces cuts/s <= 0.83, so a ceiling near 0.8 would fire on almost nothing the floor missed — and the kept cuts run 0.24-0.45 against 0.56 for the bad one, far too narrow a gap to put a blocking threshold through. review.py still prints it.

monologue.note: How much of ONE continuous take to camera has to survive as a performance. Round B, 2026-08-23: the footage was chosen because it held a 63-second take, and what separated four drivers was whether they let it stay one thing — kept 38.2s in 3 pieces, 28.7s in 5, 10.2s in 11, 6.0s. Those numbers fall in exactly the viewer's order, and mean piece length separates them 6x (12.7s and 5.7s against 0.93s). Applies ONLY to a source carrying a verbatim caption (sync.verbatim_styles), so an event cut with no speech never reaches it and a B-roll clip reused all afternoon is not a monologue.

sync.note: Only styles listed in verbatim_styles are checked — Note/Hook are authored. Thresholds calibrated on a reviewed edit: worst legitimate coverage 0.67 (lines where a confident ASR mishearing was corrected), worst head 0, worst lag 0.56s. words.json must be in TIMELINE time, schema [{text,start,end,probability}].

delivery.min_bits_per_pixel_note: HOUSE RULE: keep the picture the user shot; file size is their call. This floor is the backstop, not the target — the default delivery encode matches the intermediate one so nothing is thrown away at hand-over. It exists because a 2400k default shipped for a while: 0.027 bpp on 1080x1920@30, SSIM 0.935 against a 20 Mbps reference, and the user caught the softness by eye while every gate passed. 0.05 bpp fails that and clears 4000k upward, so someone who deliberately sets YIIBU_DELIVERY_BITRATE low still gets warned before shipping something visibly soft.

audio_policy.note: Which segments keep their original audio and which hand the stretch to the music. 'full' is the old behaviour — original audio under the whole video — and it is correct when someone is TALKING TO CAMERA. It is wrong on a 花絮 where nobody narrates: the 0820 莫宰羊 build ran 48s of continuous restaurant hum under the bed and the user's verdict was '音樂反而變得很小聲，但實際上影片裡根本沒有人在說話'. Room tone is not the soundtrack; the sizzle is, the boil is, someone laughing is. 'selective' makes it a per-segment editorial call that has to be WRITTEN DOWN in audio_policy.json — modules/audio_scout.py supplies the evidence, a person supplies the decision, gate_audio_policy checks a decision was made for every segment and that the render applied it.
audio_policy.mute_note: -20 dB, not digital silence. Hard zero is the literal reading of '靜音' and the wrong construction: the no-music sibling would carry true dead air, and that sibling is what gate_music_bed and gate_duck SUBTRACT to find the bed. Under a bed at full level -20 dB is inaudible, which is the mute the viewer actually experiences.
audio_policy.min_applied_db_note: How much quieter the muted spans must measure than the kept ones on the finished no-music file. This is what catches a build that DECLARES a policy and then renders without it — the declaration and the audio agreeing is the only part of this a machine can check.
